back: DNA made by joining DNA from two or more different sources, often different species.
Enzyme that cuts both DNA strands at a specific (often palindromic) recognition sequence.
Single-stranded overhangs from staggered cuts; same enzyme → complementary ends that base-pair.
Forms phosphodiester bonds between sugar-phosphate backbones, sealing DNA fragments.
Makes cDNA from an mRNA template; cDNA has no introns.

front: Three ways to obtain a gene
back: Cut from donor DNA; make cDNA from mRNA (reverse transcriptase); synthesise chemically from the sequence.

front: Why transfer a promoter with the gene?
back: So the host's RNA polymerase binds and transcribes it; can also control where/when it is expressed.
Green fluorescent protein glows under blue/UV light, showing which cells were transformed and express the gene.
Guide RNA pairs with target DNA; Cas9 cuts both strands; repair inserts, deletes or replaces bases.
Linear DNA: n cuts → n + 1 fragments. Circular plasmid: n cuts → n fragments.
